## Decisions taken, and what was built {#sec-next-built}

: The decisions, as taken on 17 September 2026 {#tbl-next-taken}

| # | Decision taken | Against the recommendation |
|:--|:----------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| D1 | The literal **search · account · cart**, shown now, each linking to a placeholder route that lands on the 404 page | Departs: the recommendation was *saved · selection*, with search at a threshold |
| D2 | **Detail, edge, back and video** views on every work, as placeholders until the files exist | As recommended, with video added; the generated in-scale view was not taken, and the scale diagram stays in the sidebar |
| D3 | **Any number of works in one order**, limited only by availability and by the payment route's largest single transaction | Departs: the recommendation was one enquiry for several works until a multi-item checkout exists |
| D4 | **No search threshold**, provided the query and the searchable text are correctly scoped | Departs: the recommendation was 24 works |
| D5 | **Video on work pages only**, for now | As recommended in effect: nowhere else carries video |

**What is built.**

- **The shop bar.** Search, account and cart on every page, in both languages,
  as icons whose accessible names are the words (*Search*, *Account*, *Cart*;
  搜索, 账户, 购物车). The destinations are placeholders by decision: each link
  is marked, its route is declared in `site.json`, and `check-links` fails the
  build if a marked route ever resolves — so a page cannot be built without its
  placeholder being retired in the same change. On phones the masthead takes the
  two rows measured in @tbl-next-budget: the short name and the three icons, then
  the sections and the language switch. `check-render` now fails on any masthead
  overflow, on more than two rows below 720 px, or on a shop control under 44 px,
  at 360 and 390 px in both languages.
- **A bilingual 404.** Every placeholder lands on it, so it is built rather than
  left to the host's default: both languages, no canonical, not indexed, not in
  the sitemap.
- **The five views.** Front, detail, edge, back and video on every work page, in
  the zero-script gallery of @sec-next-recs, with thumbnails always visible. The
  image pipeline makes a labelled placeholder at a sensible proportion for each
  missing view — square for detail, 3:4 for the edge, the work's own ratio for the
  back, 4:5 for video — and a real photograph replaces it on the next build and
  keeps its own proportions, read from a size manifest rather than assumed. One
  4.8 KB placeholder clip serves every work until its own video exists, so the
  preview build needs no video tooling. Video is never preloaded and never plays
  by itself.
- **Checked in a browser.** The gallery script was driven headlessly: a
  thumbnail scrolls its view into place, marks it current and adds no history
  entry; Home and End work along the thumbnails. `check-render` now measures 164
  painting and video boxes across the four widths, and eight new assertions
  (H-01 to H-06) cover the rest; an autoplaying video and a built cart page each
  fail them by name.

**What is not built, and is specified instead.** The cart, search and account
behind the placeholders. The README's *Scripting still needed* sets out each —
state, availability checks, the transaction ceiling, the searchable fields and
query rules, and why an account needs a back end — so the next build starts from
a specification rather than from this discussion. The transaction ceiling is
declared per entity as `maxTransactionUSD` and is `NEEDS-INPUT` on both routes:
no figure for it has been established.

**The shop bar is icons only at every width.** The research in
@sec-next-research favours visible words beside icons; the reference Priscilla
chose shows icons alone, and that is what was built. Only the magnifying glass
is close to universal. If the account or cart icon proves ambiguous in use, the
labels are one CSS change away: the words are already in the markup.

| 6.3 | Overselling defence extended to carts | A work in two carts cannot be paid for twice | M |
| 6.4 | Order confirmation and withdrawal information per order | Reviewed against @sec-returns and @sec-disclosure | M |

Throughout: the report updated with each phase, screenshots re-taken by
`shots.sh`, and nothing marked done without its check.

## A verification fault found while scoping {#sec-next-harness}

Measuring the masthead for @tbl-next-budget turned up a fault in how this project
had been checking phone layouts. **Headless Chrome will not lay a page out
narrower than 500 px.** Asked for 390 px, it lays the page out at 500 and the
screenshot simply crops the left 390. Every headless "390 px" result before
this part — including the phone screenshot in @sec-built and the 390 px pass of
`check-render.mjs` — was a 500 px layout.

Phone widths are now measured inside an iframe of exactly that width, which is
a true viewport, and `check-render` asserts the width it actually received. A
second trap followed immediately: inside the iframe Chrome drew a 15 px desktop
scrollbar, so "360 px" left 345 px for the page and appeared to show the
language switch wrapping onto its own line. No phone has that scrollbar; with it
hidden the masthead fits, and the check now measures *content* width so the
same artefact would fail loudly instead of passing as a finding. `check-render`
now covers 1440, 900, 390 and 360 px, and a defect confined to widths under
400 px — which the old check could not see — fails it by name.

[^apg-carousel]: W3C, [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/).
[^nng-icons]: Nielsen Norman Group, [Icon usability](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/icon-usability/).
[^baymard-search]: Baymard Institute, [E-commerce search field design and its implications](https://baymard.com/blog/search-field-design).
[^nng-wish]: Nielsen Norman Group, [Wishlist or shopping cart? Saving products for later](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/wishlist-or-cart/).
[^ucpd]: Directive 2005/29/EC, Annex I, point 7.

# Open items {#sec-open}

Five places where the evidence is thinner than the recommendation resting on
it. Every one needs a person outside this project — a customs broker, a tax
adviser, a carrier, Airwallex — and none can be closed by writing more code.

: Unresolved, in rough order of cost if wrong {#tbl-open}

| # | Item | Status | What to do |
|:--|:-------|:----------|:----------|
| 1 | Cultural-relics export appraisal | **Not established.** Chinese government sources unreachable | Confirm a living artist's new work is not 文物 before the first export |
| 2 | EU reduced art VAT rates | **Unverified.** Directive (EU) 2022/542 changed art VAT from 2025 | Do not publish per-country rates yet |
| 3 | Carrier costs and insurance from China | No verified figures | Needed before the shipping page is final |
| 4 | Export declaration for a \$300 painting | Not established | Also determines what supports the bank's FX check |
| 5 | Airwallex + HK sole proprietorship | Entity list verified for account opening only | Ask before incorporating |

## Closed since the first draft {#sec-closed}

Three items that were open have been settled in the build itself.

: Closed, and where {#tbl-closed}

| Item | Resolution | Where |
|:-----|:----------|:---------|
| CJK webfont strategy | The display face is subset to the ~100 characters that appear in headings, work titles and UI labels: **34 KB, from a 24 MB face.** `unicode-range` gates the fetch, so an English page never downloads it, and a character added before the next build falls through to the system face rather than rendering as tofu. Chinese body prose is deliberately not webfont-served. | `scripts/build-fonts-cjk.py` |
| Leonardo's hatching angle | Recorded in the stylesheet as a measurement rather than a citation, with the caveat that two chalk sheets ran the other way | `src/styles/base.css` |
| Mona Lisa glaze layer count | The thickness is cited; the count is not, and the comment says why | `src/styles/tokens.css` |
| No logo | A mark that carries no letterforms, so one file serves both locales, generated from a single geometry for the tab, the home screen, the masthead and this document | `scripts/mark.mjs` |
| The report's own Chinese subset | Was built by hand, with `cjk-chars.txt` recording what somebody had built and nothing checking it still matched the prose. It is now derived from the `.qmd` on every build, and instanced to Regular first — subsetting the variable original silently yields **ExtraLight**, which is what the statutory quotations would have been set in | `docs/report/fonts.py` |
| Phone-width verification | Headless Chrome lays out at no less than 500 px, so every "390 px" check and capture had been a cropped 500 px layout. Phone widths are now laid out in an iframe of the stated width and the received width is asserted (@sec-next-harness) | `scripts/check-render.mjs` |
| The report's screenshots | Were taken by hand in a section that claims to show what the build produces. Now taken from `dist/` by script | `docs/report/shots.sh` |

## Content still outstanding

The build reports every placeholder; 98 fields are still `NEEDS-INPUT`, 48 of them the alt text owed for the new views. Every one a reader could see is also flagged on the page in red on its own pink ground — its own ground, because red directly on the dark footer would be unreadable (5.91:1 as flagged) — and the flag is added around the placeholder word itself, so filling the field removes it with no other change. Supplying one title took that work's page from ten flags to seven. Placeholders in alt text, page titles and link previews cannot carry a mark and stay on the build's list; assertion J-01 checks that every visible one is flagged and that no mark lands inside an attribute. The
blocking ones are the photographs, the titles and descriptions, and the contact
details — the email and phone are not optional, they are the consumer-law
requirement in @sec-disclosure.

One design item is also still open. The Chinese-locale enquiry route should be
WeChat rather than a `mailto:`, and that needs a QR image that does not exist
yet; the label was fixed, the channel was not.

# Appendix: sources and method {.unnumbered #sec-method}

```{=latex}
\markboth{Appendix: sources and method}{Appendix: sources and method}
```

**Colour.** Ratios computed with the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula. The
draft's values were extracted from the PDF content stream rather than sampled
from a render, so they are declared values. Figures in this document read the
project's live token file.

**Fonts.** Built with fonttools 4.59.1 from the variable originals; byte counts
are measured output, not estimates.

**Reachability from mainland China.** Measured against a GFW measurement
service, with known-blocked controls validating the method before any result was
accepted.

**Regulatory material.** Chinese provisions read from `gov.cn` and
`safe.gov.cn`; EU instruments from the Publications Office; US tariff treatment
from the HTSUS and the Federal Register. Article numbers are given so each can
be checked.

**Layout.** Verified by headless screenshot at 1440 px and at phone widths,
not by description. Before @sec-next-harness, headless captures labelled 390 px
were 500 px layouts cropped to 390; phone widths are now laid out in an iframe
of the stated width. Three defects were found that way and are recorded in the commit
history. The captures in @sec-built are taken from `dist/` by
`docs/report/shots.sh` as part of this document's build, so they cannot show a
version of the site that is no longer shipping.

**The mark.** @fig-logo and the mark in this document's footer are both drawn
from `mark.mjs`, the one file the site's icons and its masthead are generated
from. The TikZ copy of those numbers in the preamble is checked against it on
every build. The hanging figure of 144.78 cm is the museum standard already
used by the scale diagram on every work page.
